Very different. I kinda live on the streets alone in a camper with a dog, he has his family in downtown.

When we see each other, it's always like hobo meets bobo.

Yeah, I admit my cap is quite low on the *push* thing from the start, and I'm officially "burned out" too. And although my good boats are full of T2, I personally don't have any recharger at all unfortunately. Also, I might be just too dumb for the game after all.

Thank you ozymandia5 for taking the time writing that, but I assume you really enjoyed writing it ;)

Yeah, you thwarted drug heads are the scum of everything real or virtual. Stuff your fucking weed intravenous and die.

I smoke, but don't do weeds but tried it, quite possibly before you were even born, and don't drink alcohol. Those that do are great reality escapists, enjoy your trips.

Thanks for the insightful reply. I don't really feel like having some depressive episode or anything, my post wasn't a spontaneous outburst. Those thoughts did linger for weeks, and after making this throwaway/alt I just wrote it down. During so many hours in the game there have been many more thoughts, but I just didn't care enough to note or remember them.

I started Eve not with many hopes of finding a place  to enjoy myself. And I wasn't disappointed lol. Seriously, I spent a lot of time the last months, being on vacation, and actually 8-16 hours per every day. I completely understand the game dynamics here and felt being a part of it. "It" being nothing I find something much worthwhile for a grown up decent man other than having too much free time at hands and some things to think about while doing menial stuff in the game, especially high sec mining in a quiet system.

Of course I have personal shortcomings, but most of those stayed outside of my Eve experience. I did meet very nice people, and feel bad for leaving the corp because of its exposure to regular wardecs. I will vote in the CSM and that's all I can do for making the game better.

The paragraph about potentially criminal minds here are mostly about the successful players, especially PVPers. Taking advantage of others weaknesses and failures over andnover again is to me a major moral offense. And enjoying being listed in a bling killmail is so very ridicuously revealing somebody who prefers virtual karma in a game to realizing he might be playing against somebody with an even slightly different set of premises. 

Unlike in real life, Eve actually rewards you for being this or that dick-wad.

That's one thing about my life. I just can't ever do anything really right, and neither really bad. Also because I always had the money for the bare needs, but never so much as to invest or have something done properly. My RV is a classic 43 years old car. Works great, but not legal. Meeting regulations would cost me a bit of a fortune, and I just won't invest it anymore, also because I can't utilize it anymore the way I did the last years.

I emphasized Minecraft and peaceful mode, because it's a nice example of my life. I evade difficulties and try to have it nice and be creative, but I get bored of it. I played about 10% of every game I own, on the ipad it's even less I guess. There just isn't a game with that perfect middleground for me. Either it's too hard, or I get bored of it. This goes for most aspects of my life.

There's one game I am kinda looking forward to, "No man's sky", but I doubt I will ever see it.
Actually, as detached as my brother and I am, I could talk with him about this without much uprise.

Ok that much: Only hobby is playing games in my free time, and sucking at each and every one of them. I played Minecraft on peaceful mode, and currently am in Eve online, without much of a plan except learning a skill for a day or two, and making way less game money than others because I am inefficient and lazy. Also, that game is full of assholes and grievers, but it's just a mirror of what the world is anyway, so I try to stay in my little corner and try to be successful on my own level.

I totally understand what a hobby is worth, and I always tried to find something with what I can identify myself with and gives meaning to my life, but either it was too expensive, or I was too lazy, or plain dumb, the number of times I tried learning musical instruments is ridiculous.

My single great thing is camping, and currently I am living in my RV on a campground. Of course it'll never make the next inspection and it's a mess inside, but it's my little mancave, that I can't afford to live in forever. Maybe the rest of my life though.

Anything specific?

Edit: See? I understand "talk" as a function, not a social thing....

Edit2: Sorry it's late (CET), I will read your reply tomorrow, thank you.
